messages:
alana: quick follow-up from the active/active residency RFC — experiment proposal below. want feedback on operator safety and legal constraints before we run it on staging.

alana: TL;DR: introduce a soft-switch penalty that temporarily reduces routing weight to a region that violates residency hints (eg, PII mismatch) rather than an immediate hard failover. gives us time to reconcile state + alert ops.

dave: sounds promising. can you sketch the failure modes? e.g., what if write doesn't land and we keep serving reads from that region?

alana: two main modes: 1) transient mismatch (network partition) -> apply penalty window (30s -> 5m) and stream alerts, 2) sustained mismatch (policy flag from control plane) -> escalate to hard swap after operator approval or automatic threshold.

morgan: curious how we detect the "mismatch" reliably. do we rely on proxy headers, KV ownership heartbeats, or something else?

alana: combine signals: proxy X-Residency-Assert header mismatch, control-plane consent flag, and KV-lease heartbeat misses. require 2/3 to flame the penalty. lowers false positives.

samir: how does this affect latency sensitive requests? if we reduce weight, will clients see increased p99 because of cross-region fallbacks?

alana: good call. penalty is weight-based not full redirect. we keep a small sticky fraction served locally to preserve tail latency for pinned tenants. default penalty reduces to 20% local traffic, 80% remote fallbacks. operator can tune per-tenant.

morgan: operator scripts? i want safe rollbacks and visibility.

alana: plan: operator UI in console shows live penalty windows, telemetry (failed writes, residency violations, KV lease age). scripts: `penalty apply <region> <tenant> --duration` and `penalty revert <id>`. infra-bot will tag the action with a changelog entry.

infra-bot: deploy: penalty-controller v0.3 deployed to staging (sha: 1a2b3c).

dave: what about data consistency for in-flight requests when we shift weight? do we risk reordering or duplicates?

alana: we avoid client-visible reordering by preserving per-connection affinity for the sticky fraction. for redirected requests we ensure idempotency: recommend idempotency-key header, and for non-idempotent ops we prefer canary slow drain instead of immediate redirect.

legal-kate: from compliance POV we need an audit trail: which tenants were penalized, why, and what data touched remote regions. also need automated gating for EU/CCPA flagged tenants so penalty cannot be used to route PII offshore.

alana: understood. add hard deny list in control plane (policy: residency=strict) which will bypass penalty and go straight to operator-only hard swap + manual remediation. penalty only allowed for tenants without strict legal flags.

samir: metrics to observe?

alana: minimal set: 1) penalty_count, 2) avg_penalty_duration, 3) percent_local_served_during_penalty, 4) failed_write_rate_by_tenant_during_penalty, 5) KV-lease-age histogram. alerts: if failed_write_rate spikes > 3x baseline for >2m, escalate to hard swap.

dave: can we prototype on a small subset of non-critical tenants? prefer a staged ramp: alpha -> beta -> all-stage.

alana: yes. rollout plan: feature flag per region + tenant. alpha group = internal tenants + low-traffic customers. will run 24h chaos scenario (partition, delayed kv, restored) and collect signals.

morgan: sample request header we should instrument for testing:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
     -H "X-Residency-Assert: eu" \
     -H "Idempotency-Key: <uuid>" \
     https://api.staging.redwood.ai/generate
```

alana: perfect. also add `X-Penalty-Id` in responses when the request was routed under a penalty window. helps audit + tracing.

legal-kate: please make sure logs redact PII but include tenant_id and penalty_id. we need this for incident reviews.

samir: edge-case: if a region is briefly penalized and then recovers, how do we warm KV/caches back without causing a spike?

alana: controller will schedule a warmup window where gradually increasing weight back to normal over configurable steps (default 5 steps, 1 min apart). also pre-warm hot prefixes by triggering async priming jobs.

dave: ok, one more: operator override CLI?

alana: `rw-ops penalty override <penalty-id> --set-weight 100` with audit log and 2-person approve for global tenants.

infra-bot: experiment scheduled: staging alpha group tomorrow 06:00 UTC, rollback at +24h. changelist: controller v0.3 + console flag + audit hooks.

morgan: I'll add dashboards and a simple playbook for on-call.

dave: +1, looks actionable. thanks for the write-up.

alana: thanks all. I'll open the experiment runbook and link the run id here when created.
